Zone II is one of five planning zones in Islamabad Capital Territory — attractions here are grouped by zone rather than by separate towns.

history.founded: Islamabad's secondary urban development zone, covering the G, H, and I sector grid
history.city_history: Zone II extended Islamabad's original urban plan southward and westward as the city grew, hosting residential G/H/I sectors, universities, and the international airport-adjacent industrial areas.
history.province_history: Islamabad was purpose-built starting in 1960 as Pakistan's new capital, replacing Karachi, and was inaugurated in 1967. Designed by Greek architect Constantinos Doxiadis on a grid of numbered sectors at the foot of the Margalla Hills, it is one of the few purpose-planned capital cities in South Asia.
